_comment: TECH-105's negative control, in fixture form. #61 and #62 are identical in
every respect that the scheduler reads - both open, both unblocked, both
with a parseable acceptance command, same priority - except that they both
declare src/shared.py. Exactly one of them may be dispatched.
#60 is the positive control and it matters more than the pair: a dispatcher
that dispatches NOTHING satisfies 'the colliding ticket was refused', so the
suite has to prove that work genuinely flows through the same pass.
disjoint.json is this file with ONE path changed. If the refusal here is
caused by anything other than the shared path, that file fails too.
Nothing here is real: the repo, the paths and the commands are invented.

issues.title: Unrelated ticket (positive control)
body_lines: Touches nothing the other two touch, so it must be dispatched.

issues.title: First claimant of src/shared.py
body_lines: Wins the file, on (priority, issue number).

issues.title: Second claimant of src/shared.py
body_lines: Must be refused: dispatching it would put two workers on one file.
